Every `tool.kind` the server's parser accepts, whether it is on by default, how it executes on a worker, how long it holds a worker slot, and its default timeout. Chapter 5 teaches tools.

*Parser accepts by default* means the server accepts the kind in a playbook with no flag set; whether a given worker can execute it is a separate question (see the note below). An empty profile cell means the resource model has not profiled that kind.

The **Accepted locally** column is not from the server: it is the local runtime's kind list at NoETL CLI **v6.4.0** (the `Tool` enum in noetl/cli executor/src/playbook.rs plus the `noop` pass-through in src/playbook_runner.rs (`NOOP_KINDS`); any other kind is refused before the first step runs (`reject_unsupported_kinds`)). Chapter 8 covers the local runtime.

> Kinds the parser accepts. Which kinds a live worker can execute is reported by workers (RFC dsl-knowledge-base Phase 3) and is not known to this process.

Kinds the local runtime accepts that the server's parser does not: `auth`, `provider`, `sink`.

> Profiled: the kinds whose execution was read in the worker and tools code. Also accepted by the parser and not profiled here: artifact, gateway, gcs, iterator, nats, playbooks, secrets, snowflake_transfer, workbook (see the tool-kind manifest); nothing is measured for them.

- **slot rule** (DEFAULT): Every command holds one worker slot from claim until its tool returns, including case evaluation and its lifecycle event emits; a slot is released early only on a failed or refused claim. Waiting inside a tool (an awaited sub-playbook, a polled Kubernetes Job, an LLM call) keeps the slot. *Source: noetl/worker@d1c9584 src/worker.rs:748-754, 848-897 (permit moved into the spawned task)*
- **no global timeout** (DEFAULT): The worker sets no wall-clock timeout per command. A step is bounded only by its own tool's timeout; kinds listed with timeout none can hold a slot indefinitely unless the step sets one. *Source: noetl/tools@v4.6.0 (the version noetl/worker pins) src/registry.rs:241-259*
- **retry config inert** (DEFAULT): ToolConfig.retry (max_retries 3, 500 ms initial, x2, 10 s max) is parsed but no executor applies it; do not budget for automatic tool retries. *Source: noetl/tools@v4.6.0 (the version noetl/worker pins) src/registry.rs:36-68*

## Kinds

### kind-agent

`kind: agent`

- Gated: off unless the server sets `NOETL_TOOL_KIND_AGENT` and the worker sets `NOETL_WORKER_AGENT_TOOL`.
- Availability: Needs the server gate AND a worker started with NOETL_WORKER_AGENT_TOOL=true (noetl/worker#398, noetl-tools 4.5.0); otherwise the worker fails the command as an unknown tool. The shared pool refuses `framework: claude-code`. A playbook-bound `tools:` entry (`playbook: <path>`) is refused before the first model call unless the worker also sets NOETL_WORKER_AGENT_PLAYBOOK_TOOLS=true (noetl/worker v6.14.0); see the manifest's worker_runtime.agent.
- Execution: in-process loop; every model call is a remote HTTP request; mcp_servers / agents entries are answered inside the loop
- Holds slot: the whole loop, including every model call and every awaited playbook-bound child
- Durability: the hosted loop lives in one command: if its worker dies the step restarts from turn 1 and children that already ran run again
- Timeout (DEFAULT): 300 s. model HTTP client timeout per request (ToolConfig.timeout default) *Source: noetl/tools@v4.6.0 (the version noetl/worker pins) src/tools/agent.rs:79-85*
- Limit: label: DEFAULT; source: noetl/tools@v4.6.0 (the version noetl/worker pins) src/tools/agent.rs:429-433; value: 8; what: max_turns
- Limit: label: DEFAULT; source: noetl/tools@v4.6.0 (the version noetl/worker pins) src/tools/agent.rs:464; value: 4096; what: max_tokens per model call
- Limit: label: DEFAULT; meaning: clamped 1-600; source: noetl/tools@v4.6.0 (the version noetl/worker pins) src/tools/agent.rs:697-700; unit: s; value: 60; what: mcp_servers\[\].timeout
- Limit: env: NOETL_AGENT_MAX_TOOL_CALLS; label: DEFAULT; source: noetl/worker@d1c9584 src/executor/agent_host.rs:50, 94-96; unit: tool calls per agent step (hosted loop); value: 32
- Limit: env: NOETL_AGENT_TOOL_TIMEOUT_SECS; label: DEFAULT; source: noetl/worker@d1c9584 src/executor/agent_host.rs:51, 97; unit: s per playbook-bound child; value: 180
- NOT_YET_MEASURED: a hosted LLM (OpenAI / Anthropic) call inside a real playbook step: **** (, ; source: )
- MEASURED: candidate small language model, unoptimised local serving, 2 generations per turn: **p50 9.2 s / p95 13.1 s per turn** (local, ; source: noetl/travel wiki Travel-SLM-Journey)
- Local runtime: accepted by the parser (Chapter 8 covers what it does there).

### kind-container

`kind: container`

- Execution: remote Kubernetes Job; returns at once with a pending callback
- Holds slot: no: the slot is freed after the Job is created (the callback pattern)
- Timeout (DEFAULT): none. the Job's timeout_seconds; none by default *Source: noetl/tools@v4.6.0 (the version noetl/worker pins) src/tools/container.rs:12-21, 164*

### kind-duckdb

`kind: duckdb`

- Execution: in-process (spawn_blocking)
- Holds slot: whole query
- Memory class: runs inside the worker process: a large query spends the pod's memory limit
- Aliases: `ducklake`
- Timeout (DEFAULT): none. none *Source: noetl/tools@v4.6.0 (the version noetl/worker pins) src/tools/duckdb.rs:360*
- Local runtime: accepted by the parser (Chapter 8 covers what it does there).

### kind-mcp

`kind: mcp`

- Gated: off unless the server sets `NOETL_TOOL_KIND_MCP`.
- Availability: Runs on any noetl/worker: noetl-tools McpTool, wrapped by the worker's WorkerMcpTool for auth headers. Only the server gate is needed.
- Execution: remote JSON-RPC over HTTP
- Holds slot: whole call
- Timeout (DEFAULT): 60 s, env `NOETL_MCP_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`. used when the step sets no timeout; clamped to NOETL_WORKER_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (default 180 s, read only here) *Source: noetl/tools@v4.6.0 (the version noetl/worker pins) src/tools/mcp.rs:78-82, 782-810*
- Local runtime: accepted by the parser (Chapter 8 covers what it does there).

`kind: nats`

### kind-noop

`kind: noop`

- Execution: in-process
- Holds slot: briefly; it still pays the per-step orchestration cost
- Local runtime: accepted by the parser (Chapter 8 covers what it does there).

### kind-playbook

`kind: playbook`

- Availability: Runs on any noetl/worker (noetl-tools PlaybookTool). Fields: `path` or `catalog_id`, `version` (integer), `payload`/`args`, `return_step`, `return_result`. With NOETL_CATALOG_PINNING on, `path` may be a catalog reference (`a/b@3`, `a/b@latest`, `a/b@sha256:...`, `sha256:...`, a source URI) and the child resolves inside the root's pin; see the manifest's catalog_features.
- Execution: remote: POST /api/execute starts a separate child execution on whatever pool its steps target
- Holds slot: only for the start request by default (async: returns {status, execution_id}); with return_result: true or return_step the parent's slot is held, polling every 2 s, until the child finishes
- Deadlock note: an awaited child needs a free slot on its own pool while the parent holds one; if both target the same small pool, enough concurrent awaiting parents can occupy every slot
- Timeout (DEFAULT): 30 s. start request; the await wait is the step's timeout, else 180 s (return_result) / 300 s (return_step) *Source: noetl/tools@v4.6.0 (the version noetl/worker pins) src/tools/playbook.rs:42-69, 237-242, 402-405, 433-488*
- MEASURED: orchestration cost of one kind: playbook hop, regardless of the work inside it: **~9 s** (prod, 2026-08-24; source: noetl/travel wiki playbook-itinerary-planner (#286); noetl/ai-meta wiki Sessions-Log 2026-08-24)
- MEASURED: child-playbook hop vs the same work inline (Firestore read: 369 ms of work took 11.4 s as a child; Places: 663 ms of work took 1.5 s inline): **~10-15 s per hop** (prod, 2026-08; source: noetl/travel wiki playbook-itinerary-planner#latency)
- MEASURED: paired A/B: provider children inlined into the planner as python (4 places turns each): **median 34.7 s -> 19.4 s (-44%)** (prod, 2026-06-29; source: noetl/ai-meta wiki Sessions-Log 2026-06-29)
- Local runtime: accepted by the parser (Chapter 8 covers what it does there).

### kind-python

`kind: python`

- Execution: subprocess
- Holds slot: whole run
- Memory class: the subprocess shares the worker pod's memory limit; stdout is collected whole
- Timeout (DEFAULT): none. none unless the step sets timeout_seconds *Source: noetl/tools@v4.6.0 (the version noetl/worker pins) src/tools/python.rs:637, 675-700*
- Limit: label: DEFAULT; source: noetl/tools@v4.6.0 (the version noetl/worker pins) src/tools/python.rs:23; unit: s; value: 30; what: remote script-source loader
- MEASURED: test/simple_python playbook end to end on idle kind: **0.66 s warm / 1.20 s cold** (kind, 2026-05; source: noetl/ai-meta handoffs/archive/2026-05-23-gke-provision-validation/round-01-prompt.md)
- MEASURED: provider dispatch moved from a kind: playbook child to inline python (HotelBeds hotels): **9.3 s -> 3.0 s** (prod, 2026-08-24; source: noetl/travel wiki playbook-itinerary-planner (#286); noetl/ai-meta wiki Sessions-Log 2026-08-24)

`kind: task_sequence`

- Holds slot: all sub-tasks
- Timeout (DEFAULT): none. per sub-task *Source: noetl/tools@v4.6.0 (the version noetl/worker pins) src/tools/task_sequence.rs:213-218*
- Limit: env: NOETL_TASK_SEQUENCE_MAX_ITERATIONS; label: DEFAULT; source: noetl/tools@v4.6.0 (the version noetl/worker pins) src/tools/task_sequence.rs:253-257; unit: iterations; value: 1000000

### kind-transfer

`kind: transfer`

- Execution: in-process (snowflake / postgres / http / duckdb)
- Holds slot: whole transfer
- Timeout (DEFAULT): none. HTTP client sets none; chunk_size default 1000 rows *Source: noetl/tools@v4.6.0 (the version noetl/worker pins) src/tools/transfer.rs:262-264, 308*

### kind-wasm

`kind: wasm`

- Availability: Runs on a noetl/worker built with its `wasm-plugin` cargo feature (on by default and in the shipped image), which routes it to the plug-in host instead of the tool registry. Step: `plugin: { path: <string>, version: <integer>, entry: <export, default run> }` plus optional `input` (sent to the plug-in as `args`). The module is loaded from the catalog. Since noetl/worker v6.13.0 every call runs under fuel, wall-clock and memory limits that are ON by default; see the manifest's worker_runtime.wasm_limits.
- Execution: in-process (wasmtime); one module runs at a time per worker process (the dispatcher sits behind a mutex)
- Holds slot: whole invocation, plus any wait for the per-process wasm lock
- Timeout (DEFAULT): 30000 ms, env `NOETL_WASM_TIMEOUT_MS` *Source: noetl/worker@d1c9584 src/plugin.rs:44, 132-137*
- Limit: env: NOETL_WASM_FUEL; label: DEFAULT; source: noetl/worker@d1c9584 src/plugin.rs:41, 131; unit: fuel units; value: 10000000000
- Limit: env: NOETL_WASM_MAX_MEMORY_MB; label: DEFAULT; source: noetl/worker@d1c9584 src/plugin.rs:47, 138-143; unit: MiB linear memory; value: 1024
- MEASURED: first dispatch of a ~1.6 MB module on a fresh pod (Cranelift compile ~99%, fetch ~1%); later hops hit the digest cache, and the drive pool pre-compiles at boot behind /readyz: **~1.5 s once** (kind (fresh system-pool pod), 2026-06; source: noetl/worker wiki deployment-specification (boot warmup))
